subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat the generic LiteLLM Vertex beta `INVALID_ARGUMENT` payload as recoverable session/request-shape state, and should that recovery live in LiteLLM/Vertex provider hooks or shared agent failover code?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is too broad to classify automatically without a maintainer-approved boundary and live provider evidence.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery after live proof
options.body: Reproduce the LiteLLM/Vertex beta payload, then add a provider-owned classifier or hook that triggers only for the proven recoverable shape and verifies clean lane/session handling.

options.title: Fold into broader session recovery
options.body: Keep this issue linked while a broader provider-rejected history/session recovery design covers the exact Vertex beta payload and user-visible recovery path.

options.title: Defer until stronger provider evidence
options.body: Leave source behavior unchanged until a maintainer or reporter captures the exact response object, redacted logs, and post-failure lane state from a live run.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery after live proof
recommendation.body: Reproduce the LiteLLM/Vertex beta payload, then add a provider-owned classifier or hook that triggers only for the proven recoverable shape and verifies clean lane/session handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected by merge/review history around provider failover normalization and adjacent recovery semantics.
